title: Trivial normalization of a normal scheme with locally finite components
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] such that every quasi-compact open has finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components]. If each local ring of $X$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], then the componentwise normalization morphism $\nu_X:X^\nu\to X$ [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization] is an isomorphism. No local Noetherianity, quasi-compactness, excellence, or finite-type hypothesis is imposed. The empty scheme is allowed.

source.place: Tag 0H7D, label lemma-normalization-trivial; Tag 0CDV, label lemma-normalization-in-terms-of-components. The quasi-compact-open formulation of local finiteness is the hypothesis used in Properties Tag 0357, label lemma-normal-locally-finite-nr-irreducibles, invoked in the proof of 0H7D.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-normal-locally-finite-components] with exactly the given local-finiteness and normal-stalk hypotheses. Write $X=\coprod_{i\in I}Z_i$, with each $Z_i$ its reduced induced component, also an open normal integral subscheme. By [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], $X^
u=\coprod_i Z_i^
u$ and $
u_X$ on the $i$th summand is $Z_i^
u\xrightarrow{
u_i}Z_i\hookrightarrow X$. It remains to construct inverse morphisms for these component maps.

source.place: Tag 0H7D, lemma-normalization-trivial, reduction to integral schemes by Properties Tag 0357; Tag 0CDV, lemma-normalization-in-terms-of-components

proof.text: Fix $i$ and a nonempty affine open $V\subseteq Z_i$. Put $A=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_{Z_i})$ and $K=k(Z_i)$. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], $A$ is a domain and its generic germ identifies $K$ with its field of fractions. For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset A$, the corresponding point $z\in V$ has $A_{\mathfrak m}\cong\mathcal O_{Z_i,z}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization](c). This is a normal domain by Step 1. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-normal-domain-of-local-normal] applies to the domain $A$ and shows that $A$ is integrally closed in $K$. No finiteness condition on $A$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0H7D via Tag 0AB1, lemma-finite-birational-over-normal, affine normal-domain calculation; Properties Tag 033L, lemma-integral-normal; Algebra Tag 030B, lemma-normality-is-local

proof.text: Let $\eta_i$ be the generic point and $j_i:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Z_i$ the canonical local-scheme morphism of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism]. Its image is the generic point, since $\mathcal O_{Z_i,\eta_i}=K$ is a field. Its source has one point by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Thus every inverse image of an affine open under $j_i$ is empty or a singleton, hence quasi-compact directly from the open-cover definition [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. The same argument applies to its diagonal, whose source is also this one-point scheme. Consequently $j_i$ is quasi-compact by the affine-preimage definition in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and quasi-separated by [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. For the nonempty $V$ in Step 2 the generic point belongs to $V$ and $j_i^{-1}(V)=\operatorname{Spec}K$, with section ring $K$.

source.place: Tag 035H, definition-normalization-X-in-Y; equation-generic-points before definition-normalization, specialized to an integral scheme

proof.text:
For every nonempty open $W\subseteq Z_i$, irreducibility and the generic-point property give $j_i^{-1}(W)=\operatorname{Spec}K$. Thus $(j_{i*}\mathcal O)(W)=K$, its restrictions between nonempty opens are identities, and its structural map sends a section to its generic germ. On the empty open both sheaves have the zero ring. This identifies $j_{i*}\mathcal O$ with the constant function-field sheaf, including its $\mathcal O_{Z_i}$-algebra structure. Hence [def-sc-normalization] and the construction in [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization] use the same integral-closure algebra, the same relative spectrum $Z_i^
u$, and the same morphism $
u_i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization](iii), whose quasi-compact and quasi-separated hypotheses were checked in Step 3. It identifies $
u_i^{-1}(V)$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A^\prime$, where $A^\prime$ is the integral closure of $A$ in $\Gamma(j_i^{-1}(V),\mathcal O)=K$, and identifies the map to $V$ with the spectrum of the structural inclusion $A	o A^\prime$. This identifies the actual normalization morphism, rather than just its source up to an abstract isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 035H, definition-normalization-X-in-Y, and Tag 035I, lemma-characterize-normalization, affine description; Tag 035P, lemma-description-normalization, integral case

proof.text: Every $b\in A^\prime$ is an element of $K$ integral over $A$, so Step 2 and [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] give $b\in A$. Conversely every $a\in A$ is integral over $A$, as witnessed by the monic polynomial $T-a$. Thus $A\to A^\prime$ is bijective: the inverse sends the integral element $b$ to the unique $a$ with the same image in $K$. Both composites are the identity, since $A\to K$ is injective. Applying the contravariant spectrum functor [def-weil-affine-spectrum] to this ring isomorphism gives an inverse to $\nu_i$ over $V$.

source.place: Tag 0AB1, lemma-finite-birational-over-normal, integral-closure equality on affine opens, as used in Tag 0H7D

proof.text:
The nonempty affine opens $V$ cover $Z_i$. The local inverses from Step 5 agree on overlaps: at a point of $V\cap W$ the inverse of $
u_i|_V$ lands in $
u_i^{-1}(W)$ because its composite with $
u_i$ is the identity. Its restriction is therefore an inverse to the same map over $V\cap W$ as the restriction of the inverse over $W$. Two inverses to a morphism are equal, since $s=s(
u_i t)=(s
u_i)t=t$. Their maps of spaces and structure sheaves consequently glue to a scheme morphism $s_i:Z_i	o Z_i^
u$. For each covering affine $V$, the glued map restricts to the chosen inverse on $V$. Thus $
u_i s_i=1$ on $V$ and $s_i
u_i=1$ on $
u_i^{-1}(V)$. These opens cover their respective schemes, so equality of the continuous maps and of the structure-sheaf maps gives both identities globally. The empty open contributes the unique morphism of empty schemes.

source.place: Tag 0AB1, lemma-finite-birational-over-normal, final sentence: affine equalities imply the morphism is an isomorphism

proof.text:
Using the coproduct mapping property [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], the maps $s_i$ followed by the coprojections into $X^
u$ give $s:X	o X^
u$ under the decomposition of Step 1. On each summand $Z_i$, $
u_Xs$ is $
u_i s_i=1_{Z_i}$ followed by its inclusion; on each $Z_i^
u$, $s
u_X$ is $s_i
u_i=1_{Z_i^
u}$ followed by its coprojection. The same mapping property gives $
u_Xs=1_X$ and $s
u_X=1_{X^
u}$. When $X$ is empty both families are empty, and uniqueness in the mapping property gives the same identities. Thus $
u_X$ is an isomorphism.
